The Odisha Udyami Yojana is a proposed entrepreneurship promotion initiative announced by the Government of Odisha in the 2026–27 state budget. The scheme aims to promote 6,000 nano-entrepreneurs with a proposed total outlay of ₹40 crore over the next two years. It seeks to encourage grassroots entrepreneurship, create sustainable business opportunities, and help aspiring entrepreneurs establish and develop their own enterprises. The government has planned a support framework that includes structured entrepreneurship development programmes, formal credit linkages, mentoring, and handholding assistance.
The proposed Odisha Udyami Jojana aims to support entrepreneurs throughout the business development process, from developing entrepreneurial skills to establishing sustainable enterprises. Its planned entrepreneurship development programmes are intended to help participants understand business planning and enterprise management. The proposed credit linkages aim to connect entrepreneurs with formal financial institutions, while mentoring and handholding support are intended to help them address business challenges and improve the sustainability of their enterprises. However, the government has not yet confirmed an individual grant amount, subsidy rate, or loan limit under this scheme.
The initiative is particularly relevant to grassroots entrepreneurship in Odisha. According to reporting on the scheme's proposed implementation, the government intends to focus on first-generation entrepreneurs, particularly skilled youth from rural and underserved areas. The proposed approach covers beneficiary mobilisation, entrepreneurship development, enterprise establishment, credit access, market linkages, and support after business establishment. These details describe the intended framework, but the final eligibility conditions, selection criteria, and extent of assistance will depend on the official scheme guidelines.
Odisha already operates other entrepreneurship-related initiatives, including the Odisha SWAYAM Scheme , which provides support to eligible young people seeking to establish or expand small businesses under its applicable guidelines. The proposed Odisha Udyami Scheme is a separate initiative focused on promoting 6,000 nano-entrepreneurs through business development, credit linkages, mentoring, and handholding support. The Odisha Udyam Kranti Yojana also promises interest-free loans of up to ₹10 lakh and a 50% subsidy for eligible youth. However, its implementation as a government scheme has not been confirmed, and those promised benefits should not be attributed to the Udyami Scheme.
Although the Odisha Government announced the Udyami Scheme in the 2026–27 budget, its official implementation remains pending. A report published on 23 October 2026 stated that the Finance Department had sought clarification regarding the scheme's implementation and possible overlap with existing entrepreneurship programmes. The government has not yet confirmed the final eligibility criteria, required documents, application dates, or application procedure. Interested applicants should regularly visit the official Odisha Micro, Small & Medium Enterprises Department website for updates about the scheme's approval, implementing agency, and registration process. We will update this page when the government releases further official information.

The applicant may need to be a permanent resident of Odisha.
The applicant may need to be an aspiring entrepreneur interested in establishing a nano-enterprise or small business.
First-generation entrepreneurs may receive consideration under the scheme's proposed focus.
Skilled youth interested in starting their own businesses may be eligible to apply.
The applicant may need to submit a viable business plan or project proposal, if required.
The applicant may need to meet the age, income, and other conditions prescribed in the official scheme guidelines.
Note: The above eligibility conditions are tentative and have not been officially confirmed. Applicants should refer to the official notification when it becomes available.

2. What is the total budget allocation for the Odisha Udyami Scheme?
The Odisha Government has proposed an outlay of ₹40 crore over two years for the Odisha Udyami Scheme.
3. Who will benefit from the Odisha Udyami Scheme?
The proposed scheme aims to support 6,000 nano-entrepreneurs. Its intended focus includes aspiring first-generation entrepreneurs and skilled youth, particularly from rural and underserved areas. The final eligibility criteria have not yet been announced.
4. Has the Odisha Udyami Scheme been launched?
No official launch or commencement of implementation has been confirmed. The government announced the scheme in the 2026–27 budget, but its implementation remains pending.
5. How can I apply for the Odisha Udyami Scheme?
The application process has not yet been announced. Applicants should regularly check the Odisha Micro, Small & Medium Enterprises Department website for official notifications and application instructions.
6. Is the Odisha Udyami Scheme the same as the Odisha SWAYAM Scheme?
No. The Odisha Udyami Scheme and the Odisha SWAYAM Scheme are separate initiatives. The proposed Udyami Scheme focuses on supporting 6,000 nano-entrepreneurs through business development and mentoring, while SWAYAM operates under its own eligibility conditions and financial assistance provisions.
7. When will the government launched the Udyami Yojana?
The government has not announced any date for the scheme launch.
